learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback. “Not sure” is available through omission rather than an answer-bearing hint.

items.title: Starting check: locate the bearing
items.prompt: A passage says a library added evening workshops to reach adults whose jobs prevent daytime attendance. New information says most evening participants work daytime shifts. Which passage component should be compared with the new information first?
options: The work-schedule link to evening access
The order in which the workshop examples appear
The author’s preference for public institutions
The color scheme used in the library’s notices

items.title: Guided practice: match fact to mechanism
items.prompt: A passage argues that planting street trees cools dense blocks because mature canopies shade pavement. A report says nearly all new saplings were planted in already cool parks. Where does the report bear most directly?
options: On the history of the city parks department
The planting-location link to pavement shade
On whether residents generally like mature trees
On the wording of the passage’s opening sentence

items.title: Less help: choose the narrow relation
items.prompt: A critic argues that digital reproductions broaden access to paintings but cannot preserve either texture or physical scale. A new display preserves visible texture but not physical scale. Which part of the model must be linked to the new display before impact is judged?
options: The claim that museums should charge less
The history of image-compression software
The critic’s use of a two-part limitation
The popularity of digital exhibitions

items.title: Solo practice: place the observation
items.prompt: A historian claims public clocks coordinated urban work by giving distant workers a shared signal. A record shows factory whistles already synchronized one industrial district. Which model component does the record touch?
options: The aesthetic design of public clock towers
The historian’s choice of archival vocabulary
The number of factories located outside the district
Clocks as the shared coordinating signal

items.title: Near exit: identify the touched mechanism
items.prompt: A passage claims school gardens increase science engagement because students observe seasonal change. A new study finds equal engagement in an indoor hydroponics group that did not observe seasons. Where does the study bear most directly?
options: On the proposed seasonal-observation mechanism
On the schools’ annual food budgets
On the nutritional value of garden produce
On the teachers’ preferred classroom layouts

items.title: Changed exit: read a condition map
items.prompt: A policy model is shown as: local schedule control → neighborhood adaptation → program participation. New information says a central office now fixes every schedule. Which relation is touched first?
options: The relation between participation and later publicity
Local control as the basis for adaptation
The relation between office size and staff seniority
The relation between neighborhood names and map order

items.title: Repair: distinguish bearing from topic
items.prompt: Passage claim: rotating meeting chairs distributes authority because each member periodically sets the agenda. New information: one member writes every agenda. Which relation should be named?
options: The relation between meeting length and room temperature
The relation between chair titles and printed stationery
Agenda control as a source of authority
The relation between membership dues and refreshments

items.title: Fresh re-entry: locate a new observation
items.prompt: A passage says neighborhood murals build trust because residents jointly choose the design. A record shows the final design was selected by an outside sponsor. What does the record touch?
options: The cost of maintaining outdoor paint
The sponsor’s office location
The chronology of mural styles
Joint design choice as a source of trust

items.title: Repair: translate the map
items.prompt: A model reads: open records → public scrutiny → accountable decisions. New information says records are released only after decisions become final. Which link should be examined first?
options: Timely open records as a basis for scrutiny
The link between record typography and reader interest
The link between final decisions and office furniture
The link between agency names and filing order

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A fresh model reads: repeated rehearsal → fluent retrieval → lower performance anxiety. New information says rehearsal occurred only once. Which relation is touched first?
options: The relation between anxiety and the room’s wall color
Repeated rehearsal as a basis for retrieval
The relation between performers and ticket prices
The relation between retrieval and audience size

items.title: Starting check: classify direction
items.prompt: A passage says all community theaters rely entirely on ticket sales. New information says one theater receives half its budget from a city grant. What is the most precise effect on the quoted claim?
options: It supports the claim
It coexists without effect
It negates the universal claim
It verifies the claim externally

items.title: Guided practice: identify support
items.prompt: A passage argues that later bus service increases attendance at evening classes. A survey finds that many new attendees began coming only after the last bus was moved two hours later. How does the survey bear on the argument?
options: It contradicts the proposed link
It qualifies the link to daytime classes
It negates the existence of evening classes
It supports the proposed link

items.title: Less help: distinguish qualification
items.prompt: A passage claims open plazas foster conversation throughout the year. Observations show lively conversation in spring and autumn but little use during windy winters. What is the most precise impact?
options: It qualifies the claim by season
It supports the claim without limitation
It coexists because weather is unrelated
It negates all conversation in plazas

items.title: Solo practice: separate contradiction and coexistence
items.prompt: A passage says handwritten notes preserve a writer’s revisions better than plain text files. New information says cloud storage prevents plain text files from being lost. How does the new information affect the preservation-of-revisions claim?
options: It negates the claim
It coexists with the claim
It contradicts the claim
It supports handwriting as revision evidence

items.title: Near exit: preserve the quantifier
items.prompt: A passage says councils usually adopt proposals after unanimous committee recommendations. Records show adoption in 18 of 20 prior unanimous cases. A new unanimous recommendation is rejected, making the record 18 adoptions in 21 cases. What is the most precise impact?
options: It negates the claim entirely
It supports the usual pattern
It qualifies but does not negate the usual pattern
It coexists because recommendations are irrelevant

items.title: Changed exit: read the condition table
items.prompt: A table states: “Volunteer autonomy improves retention when coordinators set clear boundaries.” A new case shows high autonomy, unclear boundaries, and low retention. What is the best passage-bounded judgment?
options: The case supports autonomy under every condition
The case contradicts the need for boundaries
The case negates volunteer retention
The case coexists with the conditional claim

items.title: Repair: match direction to scope
items.prompt: Claim: all 20 neighborhood newsletters in a directory publish monthly. The directory shows that 16 publish monthly and 4 publish quarterly. Which classification follows from the supplied counts?
options: Qualification
Universal negation
Direct support
Topical coexistence

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify a new case
items.prompt: A passage says every sculpture in a garden was commissioned for that site. A ledger identifies one sculpture moved there from a train station. What is the effect on the quoted claim?
options: It supports the site-specific claim
It negates the universal claim
It only narrows the claim by season
It coexists because both are sculptures

items.title: Repair: read the condition precisely
items.prompt: Conditional claim: shared studios improve collaboration only when artists overlap in their working hours. A studio has shared space but no schedule overlap and shows no new collaboration. How does the case bear on the claim?
options: It contradicts the overlap condition
It supports collaboration without overlap
It coexists with the conditional claim
It negates the existence of studios

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A model says a reminder improves attendance when it arrives at least one day before an event. A same-hour reminder produces no attendance change. Which judgment is best?
options: The case supports reminders at any time
The case contradicts advance notice
The case negates event attendance
The case coexists with the timing condition

items.title: Starting check: choose a bounded revision
items.prompt: A passage claims a reading room is quiet throughout every weekday. New information says construction makes it noisy on Fridays. Which revision is best bounded?
options: The room is quiet on weekdays except Fridays
The room is never quiet
Construction always improves reading rooms
Weekday schedules are unreliable everywhere

items.title: Guided practice: preserve the mechanism
items.prompt: A passage argues that free outdoor concerts increase park use when weather is mild. New information says attendance falls during heavy rain. Which revision best preserves the model?
options: Outdoor concerts never affect park use
Free concerts raise park use in favorable weather
Rain is the only reason people visit parks
All cultural events should move indoors

items.title: Less help: revise only what changed
items.prompt: A passage says shared tools reduce every workshop’s start-up costs. In a set of 20 workshops, shared tools reduced start-up costs for 14, while 6 specialized workshops still had to buy custom tools. Which revision is most precise?
options: Shared tools eliminate all workshop expenses
Custom tools never affect start-up costs
Shared tools reduce many workshop start-up costs
Specialized workshops should stop opening

items.title: Solo practice: retain unaffected support
items.prompt: A passage argues that rotating exhibits encourage repeat visits because visitors expect novelty. New information says one permanent exhibit also draws repeat visitors through monthly demonstrations. Which revision is best?
options: Only permanent exhibits encourage repeat visits
Rotating exhibits prevent demonstrations
Repeat visits have no identifiable cause
Novelty and demonstrations can both prompt visits

items.title: Near exit: revise a scoped claim
items.prompt: A passage says neighborhood surveys improve planning because residents identify local needs. New information says surveys with only yes/no questions miss newly emerging concerns. Which revision is best?
options: Expressive surveys can reveal unlisted local needs
All surveys make planning worse
Resident input is irrelevant to local planning
New concerns can be found only by outside experts

items.title: Changed exit: revise one argument-map link
items.prompt: Baseline map: local archives → access to records → stronger community history; volunteer indexing → easier search. New information says the archive remains local and indexed, but its records are available only to staff. Which revision best fits?
options: Volunteer indexing always weakens community history
Local records strengthen history when accessible
Local archives should be replaced by national archives
Record access has no relation to community history

items.title: Repair: make the smallest edit
items.prompt: Original claim: all evening lectures attract larger audiences than afternoon lectures. Attendance records cover 20 matched evening-afternoon pairs: the evening lecture drew more people in 19 pairs and fewer in 1 pair. Which edit is minimally sufficient?
options: Afternoon lectures always attract larger audiences
Lecture time never affects audience size
Most evening lectures draw larger audiences
Every evening lecture should be canceled

items.title: Fresh re-entry: revise a new claim
items.prompt: Original claim: public benches increase plaza use at all hours. New information: use rises after benches are installed during daylight, but not after midnight. Which revision is best?
options: Benches never affect plaza use
Midnight use determines all plaza design
Plazas should remove every bench
Benches increase plaza use during daylight hours

items.title: Repair: preserve untouched links
items.prompt: Map: clear labels → easier navigation → longer visits; shaded paths → summer comfort. New information says the labels are clear but placed too high for many visitors to read. Which revision preserves unaffected links?
options: Readable labels aid navigation; shade aids comfort
Shaded paths cause unreadable labels
Navigation never affects visit length
The entire visitor model must be discarded

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: Map: open rehearsal → community feedback → revised performance; printed programs → audience context. New information says rehearsal was open, but comments were collected after the final performance. Which revision is best?
options: Printed programs prevent community feedback
Feedback shapes revision; programs add context
Open rehearsals never serve a purpose
Community comments should replace every performance

items.title: Starting check: preserve the thesis
items.prompt: A passage argues that neighborhood newsletters strengthen civic participation by reporting local decisions in accessible language. Which addition would alter that argument least?
options: Local decisions should never be reported to residents
Accessible language prevents civic participation
Some newsletters also list local events
Only national newspapers can discuss public decisions

items.title: Guided practice: compare change budgets
items.prompt: Model: a guided art-walk route focuses observation, and focused observation helps residents notice overlooked streets. Addition A says guides give a brief building date after each observation stop. Addition B says half the route replaces observation with an indoor summary. Which judgment uses the smaller change budget?
options: B, because replacing observation leaves every link intact
Both additions preserve every link equally
A and B both require replacing the thesis
A; it adds context and preserves both links

items.title: Less help: ignore surface overlap
items.prompt: A passage argues shared kitchens build cooperation because neighbors coordinate limited counter space. Which addition alters the argument least?
options: Some kitchens also coordinate shared pantry shelves
Counter space has a polished stone surface
Neighbors never cooperate in shared spaces
Private kitchens are the only legitimate kitchens

items.title: Solo practice: select the least-altering addition
items.prompt: Model: rotating committee roles gives members varied responsibilities, which broadens participation. Addition A says experienced members answer questions after a new role-holder performs the role. Addition B says a permanent chair keeps all decision tasks. Which addition changes the model least?
options: B, because permanent control preserves rotation
A; support follows role performance
Both require deleting the participation link
B, because removing varied responsibility is peripheral

items.title: Near exit: compare compatible additions
items.prompt: Model: museum objects are connected to neighborhood stories, and those stories deepen local understanding. Addition A lets residents record memories that curators label as supplemental stories. Addition B removes neighborhood stories from half the exhibits and uses generic chronology. Which addition alters the thesis least?
options: B, because generic chronology preserves the story link
Both additions change the two links equally
A; it extends stories without removing a link
A, because every resident memory must replace curator context

items.title: Changed exit: use the relation matrix
items.prompt: Model links: open meetings → visible decisions; plain-language minutes → public understanding; archived named votes → later accountability. Candidate additions are: A, close the decision segment; B, archive vote totals without names; C, add a brief glossary to the minutes. Which candidate consumes the smallest central change budget?
options: A, because closing decisions preserves visibility
B, because removing names leaves accountability unchanged
A and B, because each preserves all three links
C; a glossary supplements minutes

items.title: Repair: test compatibility first
items.prompt: Repair cue: mark whether an addition preserves or replaces repeated group rehearsal as the choir’s connection mechanism. Addition A adds a shared meal after rehearsal. Addition B replaces every second rehearsal with a meal. Which has the lower central change cost?
options: A; rehearsal stays repeated
B, because replacing rehearsal cannot affect its repetition
Both, because any meal deletes the connection thesis
B, because central mechanisms receive less weight than additions

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare new additions
items.prompt: Fresh model: repair cafés teach residents to fix appliances, and successful repair reduces waste. Addition A lends basic tools between sessions. Addition B replaces repair instruction with an appliance-swap table. Which addition changes the model least?
options: B, because removing instruction preserves the teaching link
A; tools support repair without replacing a link
Both, because any new service reverses waste reduction
B, because replacement always costs less than supplementation

items.title: Repair: weight central relations
items.prompt: Repair cue: weight each map relation separately—public map → route awareness; clear symbols → quick interpretation; update dates → trust. Candidate A makes symbols decorative rather than clear. Candidate B removes update dates. Candidate C adds optional landmark names. Which has the lowest change cost?
options: A, because decorative symbols preserve quick interpretation
B, because trust does not appear in the model
C; landmarks supplement the map
A and B, because breaking one link costs zero

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: Fresh model: shared workshop → pooled equipment; posted schedule → fair access; safety briefing → fewer preventable errors. Candidate A replaces the schedule with first-come access. Candidate B makes the safety briefing optional. Candidate C reserves a cleanup period after work. Which has the lowest change cost?
options: A, because first-come access preserves the posted-schedule link
B, because an optional briefing cannot affect preventable errors
A and B, because each preserves every stated relation
C; cleanup follows all three mechanisms
